comparison: Perfect agreement on C9. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the characterization of FG-cells as having narrower waveforms supported by statistical evidence (Chi-squared test). Both rate this as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on C12-C13. Both evaluations find the behavioral controls (stable running parameters, head direction) adequately supported. Both rate as SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers noting these were part of controls added in revision.

Perfect agreement on C20-C25. Both find the control analyses demonstrating no basic spatial coding differences between cell types to be well-supported. Both rate as SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers noting these were part of improvements in revision.
Perfect agreement on C26-C28. Both evaluations find the gamma phase dynamics and developmental progression of slow gamma phase precession well-supported by statistical tests. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on C29-C31. Both find the slow gamma phase precession analysis and its development across laps supported by appropriate statistical tests and controls. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on C32-C33. Both evaluations find the differential behavior between FG-cells and NFG-cells in phase precession to be a key, well-supported finding. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on C34-C37. Both find the correlation analysis linking slow gamma phase precession to theta sequence structure adequately supported. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

High agreement on C4-C8 (shared). Both find the identification and characterization of FG-cells well-supported. OpenEval also includes C3 in this result. Both rate as SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers describing evidence as 'solid.'

Substantial agreement on C10-C11, C14-C16 (shared). Both find the exclusion analysis and sequence development findings well-supported. Peer review also includes C17-C19 (dose-response relationship). Both rate as SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers noting this is central evidence.

Partial overlap on C17-C19. OpenEval finds the dose-response relationship well-supported as a separate result. Peer review groups these claims with C10-C11, C14-C16 as part of the central evidence. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on C1-C2, C62-C71 (methodological details about subjects, housing, behavioral paradigm, surgery, data acquisition, spike sorting). Both find these methods adequately described and supported. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on C72-C83 (analytical methods). Both evaluations find the methodological details sufficient and standard for the field. Peer review groups all methods together (C1-C83), while OpenEval separates experimental and analytical methods. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Substantial agreement on C84-C86, C88, C94-C96 (main findings summary). Both find these interpretive claims adequately supported by experimental results. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers explicitly state 'solid evidence supports' the main claims.

High agreement on C38-C61 (background literature claims). Both find these contextual claims appropriately cited and consistent with established literature. Both rate as SUPPORTED, though OpenEval notes accuracy cannot be fully verified without examining original sources.

Key disagreement on C97-C100, C108-C112 (speculative mechanistic interpretations). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly speculative and go beyond what is directly demonstrated. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, finding interpretations reasonable given the data. This represents the main divergence between evaluations.

Disagreement on C89-C93. OpenEval groups these with other speculative claims (C87-C112) and rates as UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers group C89-C93 with main findings (C84-C96) and rate as SUPPORTED, stating conclusions are adequately supported.

Disagreement on C87. OpenEval includes C87 in speculative interpretations rated as UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers treat C87 as a hypothesis explicitly tested and supported by experimental results, rating as SUPPORTED.

Minor overlap on C101-C102, C104-C107. OpenEval groups these with speculative interpretations (UNCERTAIN). Peer reviewers group these with background literature claims (SUPPORTED), suggesting different categorization of these contextual claims.
